findings.evidence: Simple.lean:69-72 cites only `TauCetiRoadmap/.../QuiverRepresentations/README.md`. Every other Layer 1 file in the same directory cites a textbook: Injective.lean:81-85 and Indecomposable.lean:69-74 both end "See Assem--Simson--Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, Ch. III"; Projective/Basic.lean:83, Comparison.lean:77, Projective/EulerForm.lean:52 likewise. The roadmap README's own `## References` (lines 479-500) lists ASS Vol. 1 Ch. findings.fix: Extend the References section with the textbook the roadmap itself lists for this material, e.g. "See Assem--Simson--Skowroński, *Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I*, Ch. III" (and/or Schiffler, *Quiver Representations*), matching the sibling files.
findings.issue: `exists_iso_simpleRep_of_simple` ("over an acyclic quiver the vertex simples are all the simples") is a classical textbook classification, but the `## References` section cites only the roadmap README and names no source.

findings.evidence: Subrepresentation.lean:54-58 names only the roadmap README; contrast Acyclic/PathAlgebra.lean:26-30 and Radical.lean:89-95, which cite ASS Ch. II / Ch. II and III for comparable infrastructure.
findings.fix: Add the same textbook citation used by the sibling files to this file's References section.
findings.issue: Same omission in the new module: its References section points only at the roadmap, although its docstring states the mathematical content it exists to supply (the `pathSpan` comparison that "forces a simple representation to be concentrated at one vertex").

summary: Nothing is vendored and the Roadmap line is present, but the classification theorem is a standard textbook result and neither the new nor the modified file names the informal source, breaking the citation convention every sibling file in this directory follows.
